source: Yannis Bakos, Reducing Buyer Search Costs: Implications for Electronic Marketplaces
used_for: Ch 1-3; Ch 6; Ch 9; Ch 23 search costs and electronic intermediaries
notes: Foundational model of how electronic marketplaces reduce buyer search costs; does not imply complete price convergence.

source: Erik Brynjolfsson and Michael D. Smith, Frictionless Commerce? A Comparison of Internet and Conventional Retailers
used_for: Ch 2; Ch 6; Ch 23 historical counterexample to frictionless-market claims
notes: Finds lower online friction alongside meaningful price dispersion and persistent brand/trust effects in the studied markets.

source: OpenAI, Buy it in ChatGPT: Instant Checkout and the Agentic Commerce Protocol
used_for: Ch 1; Ch 4-5; Ch 7; Ch 14-15 live agentic checkout infrastructure
notes: Establishes a real 2025 agentic-commerce deployment; vendor source, so adoption and welfare claims require independent evidence.

source: Stripe, Introducing our agentic commerce solutions
used_for: Ch 1; Ch 4-5; Ch 12; Ch 15 ACP payments and merchant control
notes: Describes Stripe's work with OpenAI on ACP and the trust/permission assumptions changed by agentic checkout.

source: Google Developers Blog, Under the Hood: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
used_for: Ch 5; Ch 14-15; Ch 18; Ch 23 interoperability and machine-readable commerce
notes: Describes UCP as an open-source commerce standard spanning consumer surfaces, businesses, payments, APIs, A2A and MCP.

source: Google Cloud, Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
used_for: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 19; Ch 23 delegated authority and payment mandates
notes: Useful for verifiable intent and payment-agnostic agent authorization; protocol evolution should be refreshed in later editions.

source: Shopify, The agentic commerce platform: Shopify connects any merchant to every AI conversation
used_for: Ch 5; Ch 14-15; Ch 18 merchant catalogs and agentic channels
notes: Describes UCP, Agentic Storefronts and opening Shopify Catalog to non-Shopify brands; commercial claims should be treated as vendor evidence.

source: Shopify, Selling everything, everywhere, all at once: Spring '26 Edition
used_for: Ch 5; Ch 15; Ch 18 structured product data and catalog distribution
notes: Reports merchant-facing Catalog/UCP capabilities and a vendor-reported conversion advantage for structured catalog data.

source: Shopify, Introducing Shopify Agentic Storefronts
used_for: Ch 5; Ch 7; Ch 14-15 in-conversation shopping surfaces
notes: Supports the claim that merchant discovery and checkout are moving into AI conversations.

source: Amazon, Buy for Me button on Amazon Shopping app
used_for: Ch 1; Ch 5; Ch 14 agentic purchasing across merchant boundaries
notes: Beta deployment in which Amazon's app can complete purchases on participating external brand sites; do not generalize beta usage to mass adoption.

source: Mastercard, Mastercard unveils Agent Pay
used_for: Ch 4; Ch 12-13; Ch 16; Ch 19; Ch 21 delegated payment identity and tokenization
notes: Describes Agentic Tokens and consumer/business use cases; vendor vision is evidence of infrastructure investment, not forecast validation.

source: Mastercard, Ushering in the intelligence layer
used_for: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 21; Ch 23 trust, services, agentic commerce
notes: Useful for payments/trust/service architecture and industry direction.

source: Mastercard, Agent Pay for Machines
used_for: Ch 16; Ch 23 machine-to-machine commerce and microtransactions
notes: Establishes a concrete machine-payment product category; long-run transaction volume is speculative.

source: Federal Trade Commission, Surveillance Pricing Study Indicates Wide Range of Personal Data Used to Set Individualized Consumer Prices
used_for: Ch 8; Ch 16 personalized pricing and information asymmetry
notes: Initial 6(b) study findings on intermediary capabilities and data inputs; examples include hypothetical illustrations and should not be described as universal retailer practice.

source: OECD, Dark commercial patterns
used_for: Ch 7; Ch 11; Ch 17 consumer manipulation and interface design
notes: Defines and synthesizes evidence on digital choice architectures that steer or manipulate consumers.

source: OECD, Stronger consumer protections needed to address current and emerging harms consumers face online
used_for: Ch 11; Ch 17 prevalence and consumer harm from dark patterns
notes: Summarizes a 35,000+ respondent survey across 20 countries; use for scale and prevalence, not causal estimates of each practice.

source: Federal Trade Commission, FTC v. Uber Technologies, Inc.
used_for: Ch 11 recurring billing and cancellation friction
notes: Pending litigation as of May 2026 alleging subscription billing and cancellation violations; allegations are not findings of liability.

source: Federal Trade Commission, Semiannual Federal Court Litigation Status Report (December 2025)
used_for: Ch 11 counterevidence on regulatory durability
notes: Records the July 8 2025 appellate decision vacating the FTC click-to-cancel rule; important correction to outdated descriptions of the rule as operative federal law.

source: World Trade Organization, World Trade Report 2025: Making trade and AI work together to the benefit of all
used_for: Ch 18; Ch 23 AI, trade costs, inclusion and policy
notes: Primary global-trade source; stresses both reduced trade costs and uneven access to infrastructure and skills.

source: World Trade Organization and International Chamber of Commerce, business survey on AI use in trade
used_for: Ch 18 firm-size and income-country adoption gaps
notes: Survey of 158 firms; useful directional evidence but not representative of all global firms.

source: World Bank, Digital Progress and Trends Report 2025: Strengthening AI Foundations
used_for: Ch 18; Ch 23 connectivity, compute, context and competency gaps
notes: Global development source for uneven AI foundations and digital participation; later editions should refresh statistics.

source: World Bank, Strengthening AI Foundations: Emerging Opportunities for Developing Countries
used_for: Ch 18 current figures on connectivity, compute and skills
notes: Accessible companion to DPTR 2025 with current distributional statistics.

source: World Bank, Global Findex Database 2025
used_for: Ch 13; Ch 18; Ch 21 digital payments, accounts, mobile ownership and inclusion
notes: Based on nationally representative surveys across 141 economies conducted in 2024; useful for payment access and digital inclusion.

source: European Commission, Digital Markets Act Developer Portal — Interoperability
used_for: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 platform contestability and interoperability
notes: Current EU precedent for requiring gatekeeper interoperability; not a claim that future agent services automatically fall under identical obligations.

source: European Commission, DMA smartphone interoperability and data portability case studies
used_for: Ch 19 credible exit, portability and switching costs
notes: Concrete 2026 examples of portability/interoperability remedies in mobile ecosystems.

source: European Commission, DMA Review Q&A
used_for: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 evolving gatekeeper policy
notes: Provides current Commission assessment of DMA contestability, portability and implementation challenges.

source: OECD, Consumer policy and digital technologies
used_for: Ch 7; Ch 11-12; Ch 17; Ch 20-21 consumer protection across data, reviews, payments and dark patterns
notes: Useful overview of current consumer-policy problem areas; prefer underlying studies for specific quantitative claims.

source: World Bank, The global internet gap: What the data tells us
used_for: Ch 18 internet-access constraints and global participation
notes: Reports that billions remain offline and highlights sharp income-country gaps; use as a current-access snapshot.

source: World Bank, World Development Report 2026 press release: AI Offers Lifeline to Developing Economies in an Era of Weak Growth
used_for: Ch 18; Ch 23 current development constraints and opportunity
notes: Fresh 2026 framing of power, connectivity, skills and institutional quality as conditions for broad AI gains; the full report should replace the press summary in a later research pass.

source: National Retail Federation and Happy Returns, 2025 Retail Returns Landscape
used_for: Ch 20 return volume, online return rates, consumer expectations and fraud
notes: Survey-based industry estimates project $849.9B of returns and a 19.3% online return rate; useful for scale, not an official national ledger.

source: European Commission, Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation
used_for: Ch 20 repairability, lifecycle product information and digital product passports
notes: Provides EU policy direction for product durability, circularity and digital product information; implementation is phased and product-specific.

source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, The Buy Now, Pay Later Market
used_for: Ch 21 BNPL market growth, loan volume and borrower obligations
notes: Uses data from six large BNPL firms for 2022-2023; market structure and regulation continue to evolve.

source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Consumer Use of Buy Now, Pay Later and Other Unsecured Debt
used_for: Ch 13; Ch 21 simultaneous BNPL loans, borrower credit profiles and fragmented debt
notes: Matched provider and de-identified credit-record study; supports fragmentation claims without implying BNPL is inherently harmful.

source: US EPA, Community Choice Aggregation
used_for: Ch 22 demand aggregation and collective purchasing precedent
notes: Shows local governments aggregating electricity demand under enabling state law; useful as a concrete precedent, not a general template for every market.

source: Yizhou Jin and Shoshana Vasserman, Buying Data from Consumers
used_for: Ch 21 telematics, proprietary data, portability and consumer welfare counterevidence
notes: Models and documents how consumer monitoring can improve behavior and welfare while proprietary data can also create switching and incentive tradeoffs.

source: Rachel Griffith, Ephraim Leibtag, Andrew Leicester and Aviv Nevo, Consumer Shopping Behavior: How Much Do Consumers Save?
used_for: Ch 22 household purchasing behavior, bulk buying and outlet choice
notes: Empirical review of savings from sales, bulk purchasing, generic brands and outlet choice; useful background for organized demand rather than evidence about future agent coalitions.

source: Bank for International Settlements, AI agents for cash management in payment systems
used_for: Ch 13 household-treasury analogy for sequencing liquidity obligations under constraints
notes: Prompt-based experiments test a reasoning model on simulated intraday liquidity management in wholesale payments; useful as a constrained analogy, not evidence that consumer agents should autonomously control household finances.

source: Visa, Trusted Agent Protocol
used_for: Ch 4; Ch 12; Ch 16 merchant recognition, agent identity and delegated payment trust
notes: Defines mechanisms for merchants to distinguish approved commerce agents from malicious bots and link agent, consumer/device identity and payment information; vendor protocol evidence, not adoption evidence.

source: FIDO Alliance, FIDO Alliance to Develop Standards for Trusted AI Agent Interactions
used_for: Ch 12 agent authentication, authorization and interoperable agentic payment frameworks
notes: Documents formation of the Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group and standards work drawing on AP2 and Mastercard Verifiable Intent; specifications are still developing.

source: Stripe, Introducing the Machine Payments Protocol
used_for: Ch 12; Ch 16; Ch 23 machine-to-machine payments and software buying digital services
notes: Describes the open Machine Payments Protocol co-authored by Stripe and Tempo for agent-native payments; proves infrastructure availability, not long-run transaction volume.

source: OECD, Competition and consumer policy in digital markets
used_for: Ch 14; Ch 19; Ch 23 consumer agency, platform gatekeeping and overlap between competition and consumer protection
notes: Explicitly discusses agentic AI as potentially expanding or constraining consumer agency and creating new transparency, intermediation and self-preferencing concerns; policy analysis rather than observed long-run market effects.

source: Federal Trade Commission, Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees and 2025 compliance guidance
used_for: Ch 8 total-price disclosure, mandatory fees and machine-comparable offers
notes: Effective May 12 2025 for live-event tickets and short-term lodging. Requires prominent upfront total prices including mandatory calculable fees while allowing limited exclusions and dynamic pricing; scope should not be generalized to all consumer markets.

source: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. and Plaintiff States v. RealPage, Inc. case materials
used_for: Ch 8 algorithmic pricing, competitively sensitive data and independent pricing
notes: Case record includes the RealPage proposed settlement in November 2025, Greystar final judgment in March 2026 and Willow Bridge proposed settlement in July 2026. Use for the distinction between ordinary dynamic pricing and alleged coordination through shared competitive data; settlements are case-specific and not a blanket rule against pricing software.

source: IFRS Foundation, IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers — unexercised customer rights
used_for: Ch 10 breakage and the economics of expected non-redemption
notes: Paragraphs B44-B47 address customer prepayments and unexercised rights commonly called breakage. Used narrowly to show that expected nonuse can be material to revenue accounting, not to claim every loyalty program follows identical economics.

source: Federal Communications Commission, Local Number Portability consumer and implementation materials
used_for: Ch 10 portability as a competition precedent for lowering a specific switching cost
notes: FCC guidance confirms consumers can generally keep an existing number when switching providers within the same geographic area. Used as a limited analogy for separability of accumulated consumer context, not as a claim that agent memory is technically equivalent to a phone number.

source: Federal Trade Commission, Negative Option Rule Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
used_for: Ch 11 post-vacatur negative-option policy, complaint rates and institutional latency
notes: March 2026 ANPR records the July 2025 Eighth Circuit vacatur of the amended rule and reports negative-option complaints rising from at least 33 per day in late 2020 to more than 90 per day in 2025. Rulemaking is ongoing; figures are FTC complaint data, not a population prevalence estimate.

source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Overdraft and Nonsufficient Fund Fees: Insights from the Making Ends Meet Survey and Consumer Credit Panel
used_for: Ch 13 liquidity constraints, overdraft exposure and the limits of optimization
notes: Combines the CFPB Making Ends Meet survey with credit-bureau data and finds greater financial vulnerability among frequent overdraft/NSF households. Used to distinguish avoidable timing errors from underlying resource constraints; U.S.-specific evidence, not a universal household-finance law.
